source.label: Composition + anchoring mining over BM&V (BlackMarsh, BlackMarsh2, BlackMarshNorth; Valenwood) with Tropical Skyrim edid aliases
source.signConvention: pivotOffsetM = placed pivot Z minus terrain Z at XY, metres; negative = sunk below terrain

anchoring.rule: Anchor is the model PIVOT (authored at trunk base / stem base), never bbox-min. Models routinely carry geometry below the pivot (willow bboxMinZ -4.05 m, cypress -0.94 m, mangrove -2.03 m, lilypad -2.33 m) which the authors let penetrate terrain or water. Snap pivot to terrain, then sink by class/species; ignore bbox-min entirely.
anchoring.evidence: treewillow01a/02a/03a: pivotOffset p50 exactly 0.00 with bboxMinZ -4.05/-2.92/0.0; if bbox-min were the anchor the offsets would cluster at +4/+3 m.

perClassPivotOffsetM.note: Valenwood is the clean signal (real slopes, dry ground); Black Marsh medians are contaminated by deliberate wetland sinking toward water and by cliff dressing.

recommendedSinkDepthM.note: medians of the mined distributions; jitter within roughly +/-50% reproduces the observed spread

rock.note: A rock's own mined p50 is the depth that matters (per-species below); the cap only has to be wide enough not to clip a cliff face, whose mined sink runs to 11.9 m (rockcliff04, n=521).

categories.standalone: snap pivot to terrain, sink per class; no host needed
categories.attachment: must be composed onto/into a host (tree trunk/canopy, cliff face); never place free-floating
categories.cluster-part: authors virtually never place it alone; spawn as member of a mixed clump with its companion set
categories.ground-addon: flat composed piece laid at ground level inside a bush/plant stack (dist ~0 m from companion, small dz)
categories.water-surface: anchor to WATER surface, not terrain (pivot at model top for lilypads)
categories.bed-anchored-aquatic: anchor pivot to submerged terrain (bed), plant reaches up through water

bmv:architecture/phitt/ashlands/tramaroo.ownerRuling: Phase 10 round-4 feedback OVERRIDES the mined convention. The sources hang this 2-5 m up a bush or cliff; in our world that read as a big curved spiky root hovering in mid-air. The owner's rule: the base is ALWAYS ground-anchored, so it grows out of the ground. Standalone, pivot on terrain. The mesh pivot sits at the arch's CENTRE (0.80 m above its base of a 1.60 m mesh), so a pivot-to-terrain anchor already half-buries it - which is the read we want, an arch springing out of the soil. The sink is therefore small (0.10 m), not the class default; a large sink would swallow the arch entirely.

attachmentSpawn.note: Per-host spawn PROBABILITY for the attachment pass (compile-time knob, round 4). Attachments are accents, not per-host decorations: tramaroot01's rate on tropicalplant01 tracks its mined co-occurrence (2585 roots vs 6508 hosts ~= 0.4); the zero-precedent vines/moss default to sparse 8-12% of eligible hosts. Multiplied by regionHumidityMultiplier at the host's region class (deep swamp/rootland dressed more than dry uplands); values are per-host expected counts, may exceed 1 for guaranteed+extra.
